expectations.description: Identifies the ceiling effect as the cause: the inpatient mean of 26.4/30 indicates nearly everyone scores near the maximum, compressing variance and suppressing alpha regardless of item quality

expectations.description: Explains the mechanism: alpha depends on inter-item correlations, which are attenuated when everyone endorses items at the same high level — this is a variance problem, not an item-quality problem
expectations.evidence: The response explicitly explains: 'inter-item correlations are attenuated by range restriction. Less spread in scores → lower item correlations → lower alpha.
